 Phantom Blade Zero's PC requirements reveal a 145GB install, 300GB for preloading, and upscaling
 Early reviews suggest S-Game's ARPG could be one of the best PC games of the year
 By Rob Thubron 
 October 26, 2026, 7:46 
 Add TechSpot 
 ▶ "> 
 Serving tech enthusiasts for over 25 years.
 TechSpot means tech analysis and advice you can trust .
 WTF?! One of the year's most anticipated games, Phantom Blade Zero, arrives in just a few days, which means the PC requirements are finalized. The good news is the minimum and recommended specs aren't too taxing – though upscaling is enabled, again. The bad news is that you'll need a lot of free SSD space: 145GB for the game, and a comical 300GB if you're planning on pre-installing it from later today. 
 Chinese developer S-Game posted the PC requirements on the game's official X account . There are few details beyond just Minimum and Recommended setups. However, in what has now become a standard in the industry, these specs only apply when upscaling is enabled.
 The minimum requirements are an Intel Core i7-8700K/AMD Ryzen 5 3600 paired with a GTX 1660 or Radeon RX 5500 XT and 16GB of RAM. The caveat is that this is still only for 1080p/30fps with upscaling enabled. There's no indication what level of upscaling this is, either.
 For the recommended requirements, Phantom Blade Zero asks for a Core i5-10600K/AMD Ryzen 5 5600X paired with an RTX 3060 Ti/AMD Radeon 6700 XT. This is for 1440p/60fps, but again, an unspecified level of upscaling is enabled.
 What has a lot of people talking is the required storage space. Phantom Blade is one of 2026's most drive-hogging releases, requiring a massive 145GB of free SSD space. That puts it between Crimson Desert and Death Stranding 2, both of which need 150GB, and Nioh 3 (125GB).
 If, however, you plan on preinstalling the game from later today (7:00 pm PDT), that SSD space requirement more than doubles to 300GB.
 The company explains that this is due to temporary files and the complete game both needing to be stored on a PC during the unlock process. Once the game is unlocked, the amount of storage it uses will drop to 145GB.
 This sort of thing isn't unprecedented. Destiny 2's The Final Shape launch required existing Steam players to accommodate almost 300GB, despite a final installation of around 155GB, because the existing game and preloaded update temporarily occupied the drive together.
 The post also recommends that Nvidia and AMD GPU users update to the latest Game Ready and Adrenalin drivers, respectively.
 Phantom Blade Zero has received a slew of excellent reviews ahead of its official release, making it one of the highest-rated titles of the year so far. It currently has a critic score of 88 on Metacritic, and there's already talk of it being a PC game of the year contender.
